title: Compose an editable Markus homepage with reusable embedded listings
description:
Design-only planning requested by Ryan during voice. Implementation remains unstarted; no code, infrastructure, deployment, purchase or publishing authorization is implied. Initial status stays open (Discovery), unassigned.

As a publication editor, I want homepage content and embedded listings to be authored as Markus composition, so that I can edit the homepage normally while shared constructs keep recent content current.

Acceptance behavior (planned, not executable or verified yet):
```gherkin
Feature: Compose an editable Markus homepage with reusable embedded listings
  Scenario: Author homepage content and listings
    Given the homepage is the ordinary page at /
    When an authorized editor changes its Markus composition using supported reusable listing constructs
    Then authored content and embedded listings render together in the existing brand design
    And the theme supplies outer chrome without a bespoke Python homepage content-assembly function
    And the listing's selection parameters remain the sole truth for rendering and derived dependencies
  Scenario: Refresh composed pages after content changes
    Given one or several supported listing components occur in an authored page
    When the page is saved or compiled
    Then dependency extraction contributes their union to the generated reverse index
    When a published item is added, removed or changes type or featured state
    Then pages matching its old or new published state are refreshed through the shared post-save behavior
    And private drafts remain ineligible independently of listing selection
  Scenario: Change or remove the composition
    Given a page has generated listing dependency registrations
    When its composition changes or the page is deleted
    Then stale registrations are replaced or removed
    And editors do not maintain a parallel per-page predicate configuration
  Scenario: Include one page or a selected list
    Given an authored page contains a supported include of one page or a selected list
    When the containing page is saved or compiled
    Then the include is scanned and parsed using its rendering selection
    And the generated site-wide dependency index is updated
    And the index is used to regenerate affected pages rather than only record dependencies
    And a collection is a selection without a required extra storage object
  Scenario: Regenerate transitive includes once through multiple paths
    Given a published page is included by another page which is included by a third
    And more than one include path reaches the same dependent page
    When the included published content changes
    Then direct and transitive affected pages are regenerated within the documented freshness bound
    And repeated dependency paths do not cause duplicate regeneration work for the same logical change
    And retries remain idempotent
  Scenario: Handle include cycles visibly
    Given authored includes form a direct or indirect cycle
    When the page is saved or compiled
    Then the cycle is reported to the editor or operator
    And dependency evaluation and regeneration terminate without an infinite loop
    And incomplete public updates are not silently reported as complete
  Scenario: Replace registrations after include edits or deletion
    Given a page includes content or a selected list
    When the include target or selection changes or the containing page is deleted
    Then stale dependency registrations are replaced or removed
    And later updates use the remaining current dependency graph
  Scenario: Apply public eligibility independently of inclusion
    Given included content exists in different publications or as a private draft
    When an include is resolved or its dependencies cause regeneration
    Then only content permitted by the configured publication scope and existing access rules is used
    And private drafts do not appear in public pages, feeds or enabled headless outputs
    And unpublish removes or updates affected public inclusions under documented missing-content behavior
  Scenario: Recover failures without restoring stale output
    Given an included-content change failed to regenerate one or more affected pages
    And a newer published version or unpublish has since occurred
    When an older regeneration attempt is retried
    Then its failure or pending state remains visible and recoverable
    And affected pages converge to current authorized public state
    And stale-version retries cannot overwrite current output or revive withdrawn content

```

Approved unified page/wiki architecture, planning only: use one page/content system with paths. The homepage is an ordinary editable Markus page at `/`; product pages under `/features` and documentation under `/wiki` are ordinary content subtrees in that same system. Wiki denotes navigation and presentation, not a separate storage model, authoring backend, publication lifecycle or publishing engine. Reuse the existing content lifecycle, publishing projection and reader-access rules; avoid parallel site-versus-wiki systems and new content types unless a concrete need is demonstrated. A page's authored Markus composition owns its editable content and supported embedded listings; reusable themes retain outer chrome, branding and presentation. Existing routes, content, canonical/SEO metadata, heading/link behavior and brand design must be preserved through migration. Exact path schema, composition/listing syntax and Markus-versus-Papyrus extension ownership remain unresolved design work; do not invent current directives or claim they already exist.

Verified starting point: AnthusAI/Anth.us-web main 5ce142cab725cbf27e30ee15cb4904dc282da0d7 web/anthus_pages.py:404 homepage() assembles Python HTML, including three recent-post image cards plus seven dated links; web/build_via_papyrus.py:470 calls it and write_generated:704 wraps fragments directly through markus_shell.render_page. web/projector.py:369 uses generated-fragment digests for incremental inputs. This story plans migration of that custom content assembly to authored Markus plus reusable constructs; it does not assert existing generic syntax or reverse-index support. Preserve current render and SEO parity; unsupported custom dynamic query handling is an explicit design gap, not a promise to analyze arbitrary Python.

Final agreed authoring direction, planning only: “include” is the working construct name, not approved concrete syntax. It supports inclusion of a single page or a selected list. “Collection” means a selection of content, not a new storage object. On page/content save or compile, the supported pipeline scans/parses include constructs, updates the generated site-wide dependency index, and actually uses that index to regenerate affected pages; merely recording dependencies is incomplete. Reuse each include's rendering selection as the sole source of invalidation selection, with separate enforced publication/access/published gates. Nested/transitive includes, cycles, deduplication, edits/deletion and retries require observable behavior, not arbitrary-code inference.

RSS/Atom feed eligibility is distinct from page existence, include membership and navigation. An ordinary static wiki/help or product page does not automatically become a feed entry. Define shared feed selection/metadata and editorial eligibility without building a separate page or wiki engine. Exact include syntax, extension ownership and selection schema remain design questions; current Anth.us custom Python homepage code is evidence of a migration gap, not proof the proposed include construct is shipped.

Organizing initiative: Markus for everything (PPY-23a743). This is one architecture with shared authored pages, includes/derived regeneration, published projection and delivery contracts. RSS/Atom and headless remain dependent on the shared foundation and post-save behavior. Incremental vertical slices are allowed as future planning, but a bespoke custom-Python composition shortcut contradicts the target design. Monitoring remains separate and linked, not a prerequisite. This architecture is now lower priority than the real Monitoring learning-loop slice; no implementation is authorized for it.
